title: [finding] `/auth/me/permissions` is silent for a wildcard-only `viewAllRecords` principal too — the class #18931 fixed only for `modifyAllRecords`
body:
Filed by the `domain:cli` execution seat (`session_01DvvamiacK328idtBYJBxV3`) out of the #18931 round (PR #18984), from that dev's `out_of_scope_findings` where it was marked **「to file」**, class (a). ⛔ Filed bare: `finding` only; `domain:*` / type / priority are triage's.

Dedupe words: `me/permissions` · `viewAllRecords` · `seedSuperUserRestrictedObjects` · `apiOperations` · `wildcard-only`.

## ⚠️ Why this needs its own card rather than a line on #18931

**Its home is closing.** #18931 names this case as its own **Option 2** and defers it ("Follow-up; not required") — but PR #18984 carries `Fixes #18931`, so the moment that PR lands the deferral has nowhere left to live. ⛔ A deferred option on a closed card is not a backlog entry.

## The reading

#18931 was: `seedSuperUserRestrictedObjects` resolved each schema **without** the export slot and skipped every `unrestricted` one, while `annotateEffectiveApiOperations` resolves **with** it — two predicates for one question, disagreeing on exactly the population the export axis created. PR #18984 makes the seed apply annotate's own predicate.

That fix is scoped to the `modifyAllRecords` guard. A principal that reaches an object **only** via a wildcard `allowRead` grant sits **outside** that guard, so for it the channel still says nothing: the object gets no entry, the client falls back to default-allow, and it renders an Export button that the server answers `403 EXPORT_NOT_PERMITTED`. Same silence, same consequence, different principal class.

PR #18984 pins this boundary deliberately rather than leaving it undefined — one of its three new cases is `does not reach a viewAll-only principal (the seed guard is unchanged)`, asserting `toBeUndefined`. ⇒ the gap is **pinned as current behaviour**, so a successor changing it will have to change that assertion on purpose. ⛔ That pin is not a ruling that the behaviour is correct.

## ⛔ Why it was not fixed in #18984, and what the successor must settle FIRST

⛔ This is **not** a "widen the guard by one condition" chore. Widening the seed to viewAll-only principals would materialise an entry for a caller the fold does **not** pull true, flipping that client from **default-allow** to **explicit deny** — a behaviour change beyond #18931's scope, and a design call that card did not rule.

⇒ The successor's first act is to establish **what answer the channel owes a viewAll-only principal**, ⛔ not to copy #18984's patch. ⭐ Entry-presence is itself semantic here: "no entry at all" and "an entry with everything false" are different statements to a client, and only one of them is the truth about that principal.

## Where to read it

`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts` — ⭐ locate by **symbol** (`seedSuperUserRestrictedObjects`, `annotateEffectiveApiOperations`), ⛔ never by line number; PR #18984 moves both.
